text:
marie: Heads up — ACME reported sudden throughput drop on dedicated pool us-west-2. Lots of 429s and latency spikes since ~09:12 UTC. They say tokens/sec dropped ~60%.
kevin: Can you paste last 10m metrics? queue depth, batch sizes, autoscale events?
jess: Support ticket #6321 has logs. Customer saw errors when burst from their integration hit 700 r/s.
marie: Pasted GRAF: 09:00-09:20 window. avg_batch_size=1.9 -> tiny batches, queue_depth oscillating 0-120, gpu_util ~30%, kernel_time per-token up ~2.1x. autoscaler triggered two resizes (scale up -> scale down) in 6m.
kevin: ops-bot, can you show recent autoscale events for pool dedicated-acme-1?
ops-bot: AutoscaleEvents: [09:07 scale_up +2 nodes], [09:11 scale_down -1 node], [09:14 scale_down -1 node] reason=utilization_drop. Triggered by policy: smoothed_cpu < 40%.
kevin: Interesting — scale down happened while queue_depth peaked. Hypothesis: scheduler quantum mismatch causes continuous batching to flush tiny batches quickly, increasing per-request overhead and causing autoscaler to think capacity is idle.
jess: Any recent config changes to scheduler or max_batch_tokens? Customer hasn't changed client behavior.
marie: We rolled out runtime-sched v1.9.3 yesterday — changes: microstride scheduling enabled (quantum=8ms) and default max_batch_tokens lowered to 1024 for some pools.
kevin: That could explain it. Microstride makes batching windows short; combined with lower max_batch_tokens, high r/s with varied seq lengths will create many tiny batches.
marie: Repro plan: simulate ACME workload (mixed seq 32/256 tokens, bursty r/s) against dedicated-acme-1. Commands:
```
# simulate burst
for i in {1..800}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rwx-large","prompt":"test","max_tokens":64}' & done
```
kevin: Run locally in canary pool first. Also capture batch telemetry: /api/v1/telemetry/batches?pool=dedicated-acme-1&range=10m
jess: I pushed repro script to support workspace. Running now on canary.
ops-bot: Canary run started at 09:32 UTC. 800 concurrent requests scheduled.
jess: Results: avg_batch_size=2.0, median_lat=420ms, p95 lat ~1.2s, gpu_util 28%, 429 count increased when queue_depth>80.
kevin: Confirms poor packing. Quick mitigation options:
- increase scheduler quantum from 8ms -> 25ms
- raise max_batch_tokens back to 2048
- increase min_batch_timeout or allow small batching backpressure
Which one to try for canary?
marie: Recommend quantum bump first (lower risk), then max_batch_tokens if needed.
jess: I'll apply config override to canary pool: scheduler.quantum_ms=25 and restart runtime on 1 node.
ops-bot: Applied override to canary node id=canary-3 at 09:45 UTC. Rolling restart initiated.
kevin: After restart, re-run repro.
jess: Post-change results: avg_batch_size=6.1, median_lat=210ms, gpu_util 72%, p95 lat 320ms, 429 ~0. Good improvement.
marie: Customer reported near-instant recovery at 09:52 UTC. Throttle errors dropped to baseline.
kevin: Root cause: microstride quantum too short for this workload leading to excessive tiny batches + autoscaler misinterpretation of utilization. Also config mismatch with max_batch_tokens.
jess: Action items:
- Revert scheduler.quantum_ms for affected pools to 25ms by default for now. (ticket ENG-9812)
- Add telemetry alert for avg_batch_size < 3 and gpu_util < 40% while queue_depth > 50
- Create canary test harness to run mixed-length burst tests after scheduler rollouts
marie: I'll file the change request and notify infra release. Also notify sales/support for ACME follow-up.
kevin: Nice triage. Marking thread resolved; keeping watches for 24h.
ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-dedicated-microstride. Linked ticket ENG-9812.
jess: Adding postmortem blurb to support ticket for ACME. :white_check_mark:
marie: Thanks everyone — great coordination.
